text.p: These are the leading stories in the Kenyan press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Zaccheus Chesoni, chairman of the Electoral Commission says there will be no extension of the voter registration exercise which ended on June 30.
- The British Broadcasting Corporation is given the green light by President Daniel arap Moi to set up two FM radio stations in Nairobi and Mombasa.
- Opposition leader and presidential hopeful Kenneth Matiba had not obtained a voter's card by the end of the registration exercise on Monday.
- Langata member of parliament Raila Odinga is sued by Nairobi residents for allegedly demolishing a commercial building.
- Opposition activist and ex-detainee Koigi wa Wamwere registers as a voter.
- The government will beef up security at the Apostolic Nunciature (Vatican Embassy) in Nairobi following the June 17 attack by armed gangsters that left three nuns seriously injured.
- Opposition party FORD-Asili says it has not totally ruled out participation in the forthcoming general election.
- The People weekly newspaper moves to block the execution of 10 million shillings ($182,000) awarded to Joshua Kulei who sued the paper for libel.
- A number of leaders from Kisumu town in western Kenya hit out at Raila Odinga for threatening to resort to guerrilla war to enforce constitutional reforms.
